items.title: Diffusers 0.42.0: FLUX.3, Fibo 2.0, Kandinsky 6, and more
items.abstract_or_text: > [!TIP] > This release brings FLUX.3 Image Klein, Bria Fibo 2.0, Kandinsky 6, SANA-WM, and RFD4-Proteína to Diffusers, alongside new adapter support, hardware integrations, and modular pipelines. > 🚨 Python 3.11 or newer is now required. ## FLUX.3 Image Klein FLUX.3 Image Klein from Black Forest Labs supports text-to-image generation and editing with one or more reference images. Both the base and step-distilled checkpoints are available through `ModularPipeline`, with an integrated prompt upsampler that turns short requests into detailed captions and supports layout instructions with bounding boxes. The integration also includes single-file transformer loading and BFL FP8r and NVFP4 checkpoints. Load the pipeline with `ModularPipeline.from_pretrained(...)`, then load its weights with `load_components(...)`. See the [FLUX.3 documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/flux3) for examples and guidance on prompt upsampling, editing, and memory use. ## Bria Fibo 2.0 Bria Fibo 2.0 supports image generation from structured JSON captions and editing with up to five reference images through `BriaFibo2Pipeline`. The integration includes the dev checkpoint and the edit-turbo checkpoint, which runs in four steps without classifier-free guidance. See the [Fibo 2.0 documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/bria_fibo2) for the supported prompt formats. LoRA loading and DreamBooth LoRA training examples are included for text-to-image and image editing. Thanks to [@muhammadali-afridi](https://github.com/muhammadali-afridi) for the model integration (#14991). ## Kandinsky 6 Kandinsky 6 generates video with synchronized audio from text or a reference image through `Kandinsky6TI2VAPipeline`. A separate `Kandinsky6SRPipeline` provides video super-resolution. The integration supports Pro and Lite generation checkpoints, including distilled variants, and introduces `PiflowScheduler` for the distilled models. See the [Kandinsky 6 documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/kandinsky6) for checkpoint-specific settings and super-resolution requirements. Thanks to @lefff for the model integration (#14949). ## SANA-WM SANA-WM generates video from a starting image, a text prompt, and a camera trajectory. Control the camera with explicit poses or a WASD/IJKL action string, then optionally refine the output with the separate LTX-2 refiner. See the [SANA-WM documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/sana_wm) for the two-stage workflow. Thanks to [@lawrence-cj](https://github.com/lawrence-cj) for the integration (#13881). ## RFD4-Proteína RFD4-Proteína from the Baker Lab and NVIDIA brings biomolecular design to Diffusers. It jointly generates protein sequences and all-atom structures while conditioning on molecular context such as binding targets, motifs, or ligands. The integration includes the pipeline, transformer, autoencoder, schedulers, and LoRA loading. Preparing model inputs and writing CIF files uses the separate `rfd4-proteina-prep` package; see the [RFD4-Proteína documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/rfd4_proteina). Thanks to [@kierandidi](https://github.com/kierandidi) for the integration (#15088). ### Other highlights - **Qwen-Image 2.1:** new modular pipelines and tensor parallelism support. ([#14976](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14976), [#14865](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14865)) - **More hardware support:** TorchTPU integration covers eager execution, `torch.compile`, and tensor parallelism. Tensor parallelism also gains Intel XPU support. ([#14039](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14039), [#15013](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/15013)) - **LoKr adapters:** load LyCORIS Kronecker-product adapters for Z-Image and FLUX.2, including Klein. ([#14163](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14163)) - **LTX-2 motion control:** `motion_speed` controls the positional time base independently of playback frame rate. Use a compatible adapter for speeds far from the default, such as the LTX-2.5 slow-motion control LoRA. ([#14967](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14967)) - **KVAE-Audio:** `AutoencoderKLKVAEAudio` adds encoding and decoding for 48 kHz audio. ([#14384](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14384)) - **Caching:** MagCache now supports FLUX.2. ([#14756](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14756)) - **Adapter fixes:** Z-Image honors the LoRA scale in `joint_attention_kwargs`, Qwen-Image applies `.alpha` scaling to `lora_A`/`lora_B` checkpoints, and text encoders correctly report active adapters. ([#15015](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/15015), [#15016](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/15016), [#14961](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14961)) - **Pipeline fixes:** preserve explicit timesteps in `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler`, fix Anima text encoder exports and standalone core denoising, and preserve the three-value return from `InpaintProcessor.preprocess` when no mask is supplied. ([#14956](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14956), [#14943](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14943), [#14481](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14481)) ### Deprecations and compatibility - **Python 3.10 support is dropped.** Upgrade to Python 3.11 or newer before installing this release. ([#15030](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/15030)) - **Modular latent outputs:** FLUX, Krea 2, and LTX-Video now unpack latents in their core denoise groups. Custom workflows should pass unpacked latents to their decode blocks. The fallback for packed latents is deprecated for removal in 0.47.0. ([#14737](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14737)) - **Hub compatibility:** the supported `huggingface_hub` range is now `>=1.32.0,<3.0`. ([#14863](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14863)) - **TorchAO imports:** having a TorchAO version older than 0.15 installed no longer breaks model imports. TorchAO quantization still requires version 0.15 or newer. items.abstract_or_text: An open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal. · Topics: ai, ai-agents, cli, gemini, gemini-api, mcp-client, mcp-server

## New Features - Save reusable prompts and slash commands in ten numbered `/presets` slots, with a keyboard menu for quick access. (#54380, #54381) - Set model, reasoning effort, speed, and permission profiles directly with inline `/model` and `/permissions` arguments. (#54378, #54383) - Preview viewed and generated images in the fullscreen transcript on terminals supporting Kitty or Sixel graphics. (#54216) - Authenticate enterprise MCP connections using eligible Codex account grants or dedicated sign-in, including OAuth clients requiring secrets. (#55334, #55859, #56001) - Mask credentials during supported remote Bash commands and Zsh snapshot sessions, including credentials from custom providers. (#54309, #54432, #56049) - The Amazon Bedrock setup wizard is now enabled by default, with API key entry grouped alongside other AWS sign-in methods when credentials are detected. (#56033, #56023) ## Bug Fixes - Failed compaction no longer leaves partial summaries in conversation history, and background compaction failures fall back without panicking. (#53932, #55581) - Resuming sessions now finds compressed histories and restores saved thread settings instead of replacing them with global defaults. (#54008, #55923) - Windows HTTPS and WebSocket connections now handle proxy authentication challenges using the signed-in user’s Negotiate or NTLM credentials. (#55994, #56000) - CLI configuration overrides are preserved when `-c` or `--config` appears at multiple subcommand levels. (#56022) - Queued prompts now wait for pending permission selections to resolve before continuing. (#55682) - Hardened sandbox checks for case-variant metadata paths on macOS and replaceable symlinks used to locate executables. (#54273, #55384) ## Chores - Reduced disk usage by pruning unused installations, cleaning abandoned marketplace checkouts, and bounding daemon logs. (#53827, #55149, #55689, #55690, #55856) - Updated the embedded JavaScript runtime with safety checks for optimized `Array.sort` operations. It supports a 128K-token context window. The model includes a DFlash draft for speculative decoding. ollama run nemotron-3.5-bolt:e4b **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.9...v0.40.10

items.title: v0.40.9
items.abstract_or_text: ## Speech Ollama can now generate [speech](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech) with Phonon on Apple Silicon. `ollama run` plays text or a chat model's reply aloud as the audio is generated, and apps can stream audio through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint. ```sh ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama." ``` ## d3 decision models [d3](https://ollama.com/library/d3) brings vLLM Semantic Router's decision models to Ollama. Give a model text, structured state, or an image, and ask it to classify, answer yes or no, or score options with probabilities. The family includes 2B, 4B, 9B, and 27B sizes. ```sh ollama run d3 "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?" ``` ## Flint on Linux and Windows [Flint](https://ollama.com/library/flint) now runs on Linux and Windows as well as macOS. ## Other improvements - Streaming OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages requests now report generation failures instead of ending silently after partial output. - `ollama launch` now passes cloud models' context lengths and capabilities to coding tools, fixing incorrect context and compaction settings. - Anthropic-compatible web search now uses the model's supported thinking setting in follow-up requests, preventing avoidable failures. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.8...v0.40.9

items.abstract_or_text: model : fix qwen4exp layer inputs for DFlash drafters (#30927) qwen4exp published the hc-wide residual [n_embd, hc, n_tokens] as t_layer_inp, but the drafter reads layer inputs as [n_embd, n_tokens] rows: llama_context sizes each embd_layer_inp buffer as n_embd * n_batch and the DFlash encoder input is n_extract * n_embd wide. Evaluating a DFlash draft over a qwen4exp target therefore aborts on the first request in llama_context::extract_layer_inputs. Collapse the streams with a plain mean before exposing them, as deepseek4 already does for its hyper-connection residual, and build the mean only for the layers a drafter actually requested. items.abstract_or_text: Multi-column on Intel XMX matrix engines refactored (#29864) * Multi-column on Intel XMX matrix engines refactored Multi-column (2 to 80 activation columns) mul_mat_vec_q for reordered K-quant and Q8_0 weights on the Intel XMX matrix engines (int8 DPAS, ESIMD), for the SYCL backend. It targets speculative decoding verification (2 to 8 tokens per step) and short prompt batches (9 to 80 tokens). Three types also use it for a single column (Q2_K, Q3_K, Q8_0). * Fixed regression bug real bug found: the first version produced NaN whenever the row count wasn't a multiple of 4 * Removed GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 activation * rewritten xmx_mul_mat 64-byte alignment and 16-byte pitch check on the activations * Implemented fused gate/up kernel One launch computes up * act(gate) for both FFN weights, reading the activations once and applying SWIGLU or GEGLU in the epilogue. It covers up to 16 columns and works for all six XMX types. * Removed the temporary XMX_NOGLU environment switch * Q2_K min-sum optimization Q2_K weight is d·scl·q − dmin·mc, where scl (the 4-bit scale) and mc (the 4-bit min code) apply to each half of a 32-weight group * Added dispatch check and GRF sweep tg128 on Q4_K_M goes from 26.67 to 28.23 tok/s on the B70 (+5.9%). Q6_K is unchanged. MUL_MAT passes 1727/1727 and MUL_MAT_VEC_FUSION 1361/1361. Perplexity at batch 1 is 5.2064 with XMX and 5.2058 without. * Renamed variables * Added 2 environment variables GGML_SYCL_XMX_MAX_COLS (default 80, any value 0 or higher) and GGML_SYCL_XMX_GLU_MAX_COLS (default 16, range 0 to 16): the largest batch for the fused gate/up kernel. It is clamped to 16 because that is the most the fused kernel is compiled for, so the variable can only lower it. * Update esimd.hpp 1. All five quant structs were repeating the same boilerplate, so I moved it into shared pieces. 2. A new helper xmx_term does one DPAS, converts it to float and scales it per row. The four branches are now one or two lines each, and the shared Cb += z * d8r is written once. The refactor passes all three op tests. items.abstract_or_text: sycl: fix CONV_2D wrong results for non-contiguous input (#30363) * sycl: fix CONV_2D wrong results for non-contiguous input The kernel indexes the `input` as a contiguous [W, H, C, N] tensor, but supports_op claimed the op for any layout. A non-contiguous (e.g. `CWHN` permuted) input was read with the wrong element offsets, silently producing wrong results. Gate the CONV_2D op on `input` and `kernel` contiguity, matching the CUDA backend contract, and assert input contiguity in the op. `test-backend-ops -b SYCL0 -o CONV_2D`: goes from 16 failures to 0, none. ```text 2006/2006 tests passed Backend SYCL0: OK Backend 2/2: CPU Skipping 2/2 backends passed OK ``` Assisted-by: pi (unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:Q4_K_M via llama.cpp) * sycl : CONV_2D cwhn=1 support Make the SYCL backend compute `GGML_OP_CONV_2D` correctly for `cwhn=1` (CWHN channel-order) inputs and kernels, so the previously failing test- backend-ops CONV_2D cases pass on SYCL instead of being skipped or miscomputed. - Implement CWHN layout support in `ggml/src/ggml-sycl/conv2d.cpp` (`ggml_sycl_op_conv2d`). - Update SYCL `supports_op` for `GGML_OP_CONV_2D` in `ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp` to accept both layouts.
